text: The access-log search answers from the entries the local decision-record chain of rwb_access holds (AC-READ, AC-DENY, AC-EXPT) and every answer names the chain and the period it covers; the end-to-end view over the central ledger is the integration story's.
why: The entry is written by its owner in the owner's schema and collected centrally within five minutes, so the local chain is the first complete answer for the events this service produced, and the sources name no cross-ledger query.

confirm: Internal audit and the tech lead of rwb-decision

text: The export is text/csv in UTF-8 with one header row and the columns decided_at, decision_code, actor_reference, capability_area, right, case_reference, document_reference, data_product_reference, role_code, matrix_version, masking_version, grant_id, incident_reference; the screen shows the same columns in the same order, the cap is 10,000 rows and the answer above it is 422.
why: Legacy AC2 fixes only that the file carries the same masking as the screen, and the audit consumer needs one fixed column order to attach the file as evidence.

text: The masking version recorded on an entry is the version that masks it in the answer and in the export, and it is shown in the masking_version column; a later masking version does not rewrite an old entry.
why: The entry records the version it was written under, so re-masking under a current rule would make the file disagree with the entry it evidences.

text: The search takes a staff user reference only; no name is accepted, displayed or logged, and no personal field is returned by either read.
why: The entry carries a user reference and the data-minimisation requirement forbids returning personal data that the audit question does not need.

text: Access entries are retained under the decision log's retention rule (NFR-030); no separate access-log retention rule, job or deletion path is built in this story.
why: The access entry is a decision-record entry of the same chain, so a second retention rule would give one chain two lifetimes.
read: Architecture v5 slide 28; TSD P4 v3 T7; NFR-030.
